title: Birbal and the line on the wall.
lines: Long ago in India there lived a powerful emperor.
He liked asking his ministers difficult questions.
One day Akbar was sitting in his great hall.
All the ministers were standing around him.
Akbar had a piece of chalk in his hand.
A straight white line on the wall.
Who can make this line shorter?
But you mustn't touch the line.
You mustn't wipe any of it off.
The ministers looked at each other.
The first minister said: That can't be done, Your Majesty.
Make a line shorter without touching it?
The second minister thought for a long time.
Maybe we could hang a cloth in front of it?
Then you can't see part of it.
Then the line is still just as long.
The third minister said: We could stand far away.
The line must really become shorter.
He asked for a piece of chalk.
He didn't touch the emperor's line.
He walked all the way to the end of the wall.
Next to Birbal's long line, his own line suddenly looked very short.
I didn't touch your line, said Birbal.
Because next to something bigger, everything looks smaller.
Why didn't we think of that?
You don't have to make someone else smaller to be big yourself.
Akbar thought about that for a long time.
That's the wisest lesson of the day, he said.
He gave Birbal a gold ring.
And the lines stayed on the wall for a long time.
So that everyone could remember it.
